subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education, KS3-KS4 core PE); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, resilience, leadership, lifelong activity) adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Exercise and mental wellbeing
objectives: Explain how exercise affects mood, stress and sleep
Identify barriers to being active and solutions
Create a plan for managing stress through movement

keywords.def: feeling mentally healthy and able to cope
pressure that makes us feel tense or overwhelmed
chemicals released in the body during exercise that can lift mood
something that makes it harder to do something

starter: Bismillah. What is a SMART goal?
What is the moderate heart rate zone?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Move at your own comfort level
If you feel very low or anxious, speak to a trusted adult
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson. Mental health discussion: use the PSHE ground rules; signpost to Childline 0800 1111 where relevant.

teach.heading: How exercise helps
bullets: Can lift mood and reduce stress
teach.note: Research shows regular activity is linked to better mood and sleep. It is not a cure for mental illness. Avoid saying exercise fixes everything.

teach.heading: Barriers
bullets: No time, no energy, screen time
teach.note: Pupils list their barriers. Discuss that online learning means sitting a lot.

teach.heading: Solutions
teach.note: Link to remembering Allah and taking care of the body: 'Your body has a right over you' (Sahih al-Bukhari).

teach.heading: Stress-release routine
teach.note: Pupils design and try a 5-minute routine. Keep modest and appropriate.

practice: Name a benefit of exercise for mood.
independent: List three barriers you face and one solution for each.
Try a 2-minute breathing and stretch routine.
exit: Design a 5-minute stress-relief routine and perform it.
Write how you felt before and after.
homework: Give two ways exercise supports mental wellbeing.
Suggest one way to overcome a barrier.
lessons.send: Use your routine once a day this week and note your mood.

lessons.title: Safe high-intensity interval training (HIIT)
objectives: Describe HIIT and its effects on fitness
Perform bodyweight HIIT with safe technique

keywords.def: high-intensity interval training: short hard efforts with rest
the relationship between work and rest time
an exercise where you drive your knees towards your chest from a plank
doing too much without enough recovery

starter: What are the signs you should stop?

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Land softly; no jumping on hard slippery floors
Stop if dizzy, nauseous or in pain
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: What is HIIT?
bullets: Followed by rest or low effort
teach.note: Explain HIIT is demanding; young people should build up. Not suitable if unwell or injured.

teach.heading: Choosing exercises
teach.note: Offer low-impact options for every exercise. Teach landing technique: soft knees, quiet feet.

teach.heading: Work to rest ratio
teach.note: Start with 1:2. Misconception: harder is always better; quality technique first.

teach.heading: Recovery
teach.note: Overtraining signs: tiredness, poor sleep, low mood. Allow 48 hours between HIIT sessions.

practice: Why do we rest between intervals?
independent: Do a trial of 20 seconds work and 40 rest for 3 rounds.
Rate your effort on the 1 to 10 scale.
exit: Complete a 12-minute HIIT session with 6 exercises.
homework: Describe the HIIT work:rest ratio you used.
lessons.send: Plan a safe HIIT session for later in the week with at least two rest days.
